title: Conjectures: computer-assisted and formally verified results on open problems in mathematics
description:
Papers, code, data and machine-checked proofs (Lean 4, DRAT) for results on open problems in mathematics. Each result states its category: A, every claim proved by the Lean kernel; B, computer-assisted, with the reductions and checker soundness proved in Lean; C, a reproducible computation with independently checked witnesses. Current problem: the Erdős–Gyárfás conjecture.

Release v1.2.0 extends the paper Every cubic bipartite graph on at most 88 vertices has a cycle of length 4, 8 or 16 from 84 to 88 vertices: a cubic bipartite counterexample to the Erdős–Gyárfás conjecture has at least 90 vertices. For the two new caps, as for all earlier ones, the counters of Branch A agree with Julius Tranquilli's unchanged program. The release adds two preprints: Cycles of length 4, 8, 16 and 32 in censuses of cubic graphs (category C: every connected cubic graph of girth at least 9 on at most 64 vertices has a 16-cycle, and every graph in the published censuses of cubic vertex-transitive graphs up to 1280 vertices and cubic symmetric graphs up to 10,000 vertices has a cycle of length 4, 8, 16 or 32) and The smallest Tutte–Coxeter lifts without cycles of length 32 (category B: a lift of the Tutte–Coxeter graph by the gadgets H7, H8*, H15 without a 32-cycle has at least 345 vertices, and at least 370 if it is cubic; a counting identity is proved in Lean 4 and the remaining cases are refuted by CaDiCaL with DRAT proofs checked by drat-trim).

Release v1.1.0 added the first version of this paper, for graphs on at most 84 vertices (category B: computer-assisted, with the case split and the soundness of the witness checks proved in Lean 4). The search code adapts Julius Tranquilli's MIT-licensed program and keeps the MIT License (folder results/cubic-bipartite-power-of-two-cycles/src); everything else is CC0.

Release v1.0.0 contained the paper Small graphs without cycles of length a power of two with its formal development: fδ≥3(4) ≤ 73, fδ≥3(5) ≤ 345 and fcubic(6) ≤ 10,498. The proofs use Lean 4.36.0 without Mathlib, without native_decide, and only the standard axioms propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound.

AI systems (Gemini 4 Neon, Claude Opus 5.5; tools Antigravity and Claude Code) assisted substantially; they are not authors.
keywords: cycles of length a power of two
